newsitem.title: CHINA: China not to open telecoms market-China Telecom.
newsitem.headline: China not to open telecoms market-China Telecom.

text.p: China is not yet ready to open its telecommunications market to foreign firms and China Telecom's purchase of a stake in Hongkong Telecommunications Ltd was a step toward becoming an equal shareholder with Cable & Wireless Plc, state media said on Wednesday.
"China's policy in the telecom sector is unchanged," the China Daily quoted Qu Wenchu, deputy director-general of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, as saying.
China does not allow foreign companies to operate telecommunications networks in the domestic market but it needs huge amounts of capital to expand its own services.

China Telecom, operating arm of the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, has agreed to buy a 5.5 percent stake in Hongkong Telecommunications from the Hong Kong company's British parent, Cable & Wireless Plc in a deal that has sparked speculation that Cable and Wireless could gain entry to the China market.
"The situation is not mature enough for China to open its telecom sector to foreign firms," Qu said.
However, he said China Telecom's purchase marked only a first step.
"The deal is only a primary step in the cooperation between China Telecom (Hong Kong) and C and W," Qu said.
"C and W will continue to sell its stake to China Telecom (Hong Kong), until the two eventually become equal shareholders," Qu said.
A China Telecom official said on Tuesday the agreement did not give any priority to Hongkong Telecom to gain a foothold in the China market.
China Telecom (Hong Kong)'s purchase of the stake was purely a business deal, the China Daily quoted China Telecom president Zhang Ligui as saying.
"The operation will be conducive to long-term cooperation between China Telecom and Hongkong Telecom and continue Hongkong Telecom's sustaintable development in the future," Zhang said.
China Telecom officials said on Tuesday the company was studying a listing for China Telecom (Hong Kong) and a listing was expected in the near future.
The China Telecom official gave no indication of the size or the exact timing of any stock listing in Hong Kong.
The agreement between China Telecom and Cable & Wireless had long been anticipated before the return of the British colony to Chinese rule on July 1.
Beijing has been eager to take an interest in key areas of the territory's economy, and has already moved into the airline sector.
